stories.title: Deadly Train Collision in Central Spain Claims at Least 68 Lives
stories.summary: A high-speed train collided with another that had stopped on the tracks in Toledo, Spain, resulting in at least 68 fatalities and numerous injuries. The incident, which occurred on Wednesday, marks the second deadly rail crash in Spain this year, raising concerns about rail safety. Local officials reported that over 500 passengers were on board the trains at the time of the accident.

stories.title: Flávio Bolsonaro and Family Granted US Visas After Election Loss and Fleeing Brazil
stories.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro, the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate, and his family have arrived in Miami after fleeing Brazil. This move follows his refusal to concede defeat to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and a court order that barred him from leaving the country due to ongoing investigations into money laundering and other allegations. The US State Department has granted them entry visas amid these developments.

stories.title: Netanyahu's Bloc Leads Israeli Election, But Majority Remains Elusive
stories.summary: As of the latest counts, Netanyahu's right-wing bloc is leading the Israeli election but is falling short of the 61 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset. With over 85% of the votes counted, projections indicate that Netanyahu's Likud party and its allies are set to secure around 53 seats, while the opposing coalition led by Eisenkot is expected to gain approximately 48 seats, alongside 19 seats for Arab-led parties. The results suggest a potential deadlock, prompting calls from President Isaac Herzog to avoid another election.

Despite high voter turnout, projections indicate that opposition parties have gained more seats, but they lack the majority needed to form a government, leading to potential coalition negotiations in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Dolores Huerta, influential civil rights activist, passes away at 96
stories.summary: Dolores Huerta, a prominent labor rights leader and co-founder of the United Farm Workers, has died at the age of 96. Huerta was instrumental in advocating for the rights of agricultural workers and is known for coining the phrase 'Sí, se puede!' which became a rallying cry for labor movements. Her legacy includes significant contributions to improving working conditions for farmworkers across the United States.

stories.summary: A minor was shot dead by Serbian police after attacking a guard with knives outside the Israeli Embassy in Belgrade. The interior minister confirmed that the attacker was underage and had been under surveillance by security services. Following the incident, authorities declared the highest terror alert level.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Cause Casualties and Fires in Kyiv and Kharkiv
stories.summary: Recent Russian missile and drone strikes in Ukraine have resulted in casualties and significant damage. In Kyiv, one person was killed and 15 injured, with emergency workers rescuing a dog from the rubble of damaged university buildings and a major bridge. Meanwhile, a drone strike in Kharkiv injured five people, including a 4-year-old child, and ignited several fires, prompting firefighters to respond amid ongoing threats of further attacks.

She had been held on remand for seven years following charges related to an alleged attempt to murder her former husband, Constantino Chiwenga, in 2019.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab Causes Fatalities and Evacuations in North Andhra
stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab has made landfall in north Andhra Pradesh, resulting in at least five fatalities. The storm has brought extremely heavy rain and winds gusting up to 150 km/h, leading to significant damage, including the uprooting of over 1,000 trees and affecting crops across 80,500 hectares. Authorities have evacuated tens of thousands of residents from coastal areas as a precautionary measure.
